Calculate tolerance intervals

Source: R/stats.R
tol_int.Rd

Calculates tolerance intervals for each distribution-estimation result in `df`. Uncensored observations are dispatched to the corresponding EnvStats tolerance-interval function. When `censored_col` is supplied and contains censored observations, the appropriate censored EnvStats function is used when available.

Usage

tol_int(
  df,
  analysis_result = "analysis_result",
  distribution = "distribution",
  censored_col = NULL,
  coverage = 0.95,
  cov_type = "content",
  ti_type = "two-sided",
  method = "exact",
  conf_level = 0.95,
  censoring_side = "left"
)

Arguments

df

A data frame returned by [est_dist()] with `keep_data_object = TRUE`.

analysis_result

Character scalar giving the name of the result column inside each nested data frame.

distribution

Character scalar giving the name of the distribution column in `df`.

censored_col

Optional character scalar giving the name of a logical censoring-indicator column inside each nested data frame. `TRUE` identifies a censored observation.

coverage

A scalar between 0 and 1 specifying the desired population coverage. For `cov_type = "expectation"`, EnvStats may ignore this argument.

cov_type

Coverage type. Supported values are `"content"` and `"expectation"`.

ti_type

Tolerance-interval type. Supported values are `"two-sided"`, `"upper"`, and `"lower"`.

method

Character string specifying the method used for parametric tolerance intervals.

conf_level

A scalar between 0 and 1 specifying the confidence level of the tolerance interval.

censoring_side

Character string specifying the censoring direction passed to EnvStats. Use `"left"` for typical groundwater nondetect data.

Value

A data frame containing the grouping columns from `df`, the estimated distribution, sample size, confidence level, and tolerance limits:

  • `ltl`: lower tolerance limit;

  • `utl`: upper tolerance limit;

  • `sample_size`: number of observations used;

  • `conf_level`: confidence level.

Details

The input must be generated by [est_dist()] with `keep_data_object = TRUE`.

See also

[est_dist()], [conf_int()], [EnvStats::tolIntNorm()], [EnvStats::tolIntLnorm()], [EnvStats::tolIntNpar()], [EnvStats::tolIntNormCensored()]

Examples

# \donttest{
data("gw_data")

background_data <- gw_data |>
  dplyr::filter(
    location_id %in% c("MW-1", "MW-2", "MW-3", "MW-4"),
    param_name %in% c(
      "Sulfate, total",
      "Arsenic, dissolved",
      "Boron, dissolved"
    ),
    sample_date >= lubridate::ymd("2007-12-20"),
    sample_date <= lubridate::ymd("2012-01-01")
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    location_id,
    param_name,
    default_unit
  ) |>
  percent_lt() |>
  est_dist(keep_data_object = TRUE)
#> Error in est_dist(percent_lt(dplyr::group_by(dplyr::filter(gw_data, location_id %in%     c("MW-1", "MW-2", "MW-3", "MW-4"), param_name %in% c("Sulfate, total",     "Arsenic, dissolved", "Boron, dissolved"), sample_date >=     lubridate::ymd("2007-12-20"), sample_date <= lubridate::ymd("2012-01-01")),     location_id, param_name, default_unit)), keep_data_object = TRUE): could not find function "est_dist"

tol_int(
  background_data,
  coverage = 0.95,
  cov_type = "content",
  ti_type = "upper",
  conf_level = 0.99
)
#> Error: object 'background_data' not found
# }
